content:
sarah.ng: Quick Q — QA ran embeddings smoke and found inconsistent behavior for empty-string inputs and very long inputs. Are we returning a fixed-dim zero vector, null, or an error? Also: how does per-item truncation work when a batch exceeds the model token limit? cc @tom.h @jules

 tom.h: Can you paste the sample request + response you saw? Was this hosted or dedicated?

 sarah.ng: Hosted. Here's the minimal repro we used:

 ```json
 POST /v1/embeddings
 {
   "model": "redwood-mini-emb-v1",
   "input": ["", "Long text...(>20k chars)"]
 }

 // response we got
 {
   "data": [
     {"embedding": [0, 0, 0, 0, ...]},
     {"embedding": [0.0123, -0.0456, ...]}
   ]
 }
 ```

 sarah.ng: But sometimes the first item is `null` instead of zeros for other runs, so flaky. We need a deterministic contract (and tests).

 jules: Short answer: we should guarantee a stable shape and not return null for SDK consumers unless the input is missing (not an empty string). Proposal:
 - Always return an embedding vector with length = model_dim for every input element (no nulls).
 - For empty-string inputs, return the model's embedding for the empty string (currently zeros for quantized builds, but that might change) — best to document the semantic rather than promise zeros.
 - Truncation: per-item truncation applies individually based on tokenized length. We truncate each string to model_max_tokens and compute embedding of truncated text.
 - Batch limits: reject requests with items > 2048 (configurable per model) with 413 / error and message "batch size exceeds limit".

 tom.h: I like the deterministic-shape rule. Small ask: can we add a header or response flag so clients can detect that an item was truncated? e.g., `x-embed-truncation: [false,true]` or a per-item `metadata.truncated: true`? That helps UIs.

 jules: Adding per-item metadata in the response is backward compatible if we put it behind an opt-in query param `include_item_metadata=true`. Default keep the slim response. That avoids breaking lightweight SDKs.

 sarah.ng: Sounds good. For the empty-string case — QA wants a clear canonical behavior so tests don't flake. Could we agree: contract says "embedding(empty string) = embedding(tokenized_empty) and is stable per model version" and we add a regression test that asserts shape and not-null.

 jules: Agreed. Action items:
 - docs: update embeddings contract section to state fixed-shape output, per-item truncation, and opt-in `include_item_metadata` for truncated flags. (I'll open a docs PR)
 - runtime: make sure we never serialize null for embedding items; if backend produces special sentinel, map to vector of length model_dim (populate with model's empty-string embedding). (assign to @tom.h)
 - qa: add smoke test that sends empty string and super-long string; assert `len(embedding) == model_dim` and for long string assert metadata.truncated when include_item_metadata=true. (assign to @sarah.ng)

 ops-bot: embed-tests/ci - run #4523: failed (empty-inputs) — https://ci.redwood/4523 :warning:

 tom.h: I'll push a small patch to runtime to normalize null->empty-embedding and add the `include_item_metadata` flag handler. Will add unit test for batch>2048 rejection.

 sarah.ng: Perfect. Can you @-mention me on the PR so QA can validate before merging?

 tom.h: Will do. ETA EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

 jules: I'll draft the docs change and include an example response that shows `metadata.truncated` when requested. Quick example for docs: 

 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {"embedding": [0.0, 0.0, ...], "metadata": {"truncated": false}},
     {"embedding": [0.123, -0.045, ...], "metadata": {"truncated": true}}
   ]
 }
 ```

 sarah.ng: Thanks. This should make SDK behavior stable. I'll follow up with QA results after tom's patch lands.

 tom.h: ping when QA green, then we'll cut a micro-release for hosted runtime.

 jules: One last note — include a small note in the changelog about the new opt-in metadata to avoid surprised consumers.

 sarah.ng: noted. closing loop here once CI passes. :white_check_mark:
